properties.headline: Gale Warning issued November 24 at 4:22AM EST until November 26 at 9:00AM EST by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Northeast winds 25 to 35 kt with gusts up to 45 kt and
seas 10 to 15 ft expected.

* WHERE...The coastal waters from Cape Hatteras to Surf City.

* WHEN...Until 9 AM EST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Strong winds will cause hazardous seas which could
capsize or damage vessels and reduce visibility.
properties.instruction:
Mariners should alter plans to avoid these hazardous conditions.
Remain in port, seek safe harbor, alter course, and/or secure the
vessel for hazardous conditions.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Watch issued November 24 at 12:55AM EST until November 27 at 10:00AM EST by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to 2 to 4 feet of inundation above ground level
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Areas along the beaches, Pamlico Sound, and adjacent
tidal creeks, and Ocracoke Island.

* WHEN...From Wednesday evening through Friday morning.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. This includes impacts
to Hwy 12. Low lying property including homes, businesses, and
some critical infrastructure may be inundated. Some shoreline
erosion may occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...King Tides will be peaking on Wednesday and
Thursday before gradually lowering which will continue to bring
elevated water levels to the area through much of the week. The
King Tides will be exacerbated by a strong coastal low impacting
the area Wednesday evening into Thursday morning. The higher of
the high tide cycles will be during the morning hours each day
this week. Initially ocean overwash will be a concern as 10-15
ft seas impact the area beaches. This will be of greatest
concern across the more vulnerable dunes along Hwy 12. However
as winds switch to a SW direction Thursday afternoon and evening
minor water level rises (around 1-2 ft) on soundside locations
of Hatteras and Ocracoke Island will be possible as water
sloshes back towards the eastern end of the Pamlico Sound.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

properties.areaDesc: Beaufort; Pamlico; Southern Craven; East Carteret
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Watch issued November 24 at 12:55AM EST until November 26 at 4:00PM EST by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to 2 to 4 feet of inundation above ground level
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Areas along the southern Pamlico Sound, Bay and Lower
Neuse Rivers, Core Sound, and adjacent tidal creeks, and areas
along the Pamlico and Pungo Rivers and adjacent tidal creeks.

* WHEN...From Wednesday evening through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Up to 2 to 4 feet of inundation above ground level is
possible in some areas near shorelines and tidal waterways
resulting in an elevated threat of property damage. Flooding
will extend inland from the waterfront threatening some homes
and businesses. Isolated road closures and flooding of vehicles
will be possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...King Tides will be peaking on Wednesday and
Thursday before gradually lowering which will continue to bring
elevated water levels to the area through much of the week. The
King Tides will be exacerbated by a strong coastal low impacting
the area. The higher of the high tide cycles will be during the
morning hours each day this week. This is forecast to bring
nuisance water level rises on Tuesday across the watch area with
minor to locally moderate impacts forecast on Wednesday. The
worst impacts are currently forecast with the morning high tide
cycle on Thursday.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.
